question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in per-message timestamps to the core TUI, and should the control be persistent config, an in-session toggle, or both?
rationale: The missing display is source-visible, but adding a TUI setting or command creates a user-facing UX/config contract that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
options.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, uses real message timestamps for live and replayed rows, and includes PTY-visible proof.

options.title: Prefer session-only toggle
options.body: Avoid growing persisted config and accept only an in-session TUI control if maintainers want a lighter surface.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Close or defer the request if maintainers want the TUI to stay visually minimal and rely on logs or terminal scrollback for timing.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
recommendation.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, uses real message timestamps for live and replayed rows, and includes PTY-visible proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest available TUI product/history signal among the likely owners for deciding the UX/config contract.
